found.title: Search engines
found.intro: Where clients look for you: Google, Maps, Bing, Apple, social media and your own website. Each reads different signals. This checklist walks you through setting each one up correctly. Tick a step when it's done.
found.noPromise: Nobody can promise a top position: Google says you can't pay to rank higher. What helps is being complete, accurate and the same everywhere.

same.title: The same details everywhere
same.hint: Copy these exactly into every profile. Different names, phone numbers or hours confuse search engines and clients.
same.name: Business name

website.title: Your website
website.why: Google (including AI Overviews), Bing and ChatGPT read your website first. They need clear pages they can read; no special "AI files" are needed.
todo: Add the booking button or widget to your website.
Describe each service with its price or price range, your area and your opening hours, as plain text.
Paste the business details code below into your home page, so your hours, address and services are read correctly.
Check that it loads fast on a phone.

google.title: Google Business Profile (Search and Maps)
google.why: Maps results are based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence. A complete, verified profile is the foundation.
todo: Claim and verify your business.
Pick the right main category (e.g. Hair salon, Nail salon) and add your services.
Copy the name, address, phone and hours from the box above.
Add your booking link under Bookings, so a "Book" button appears.
Add real photos of the salon and your work.

searchConsole.title: Google Search Console
searchConsole.why: Shows whether Google can find and index your website, and what people search to find you. Only if you have your own website.
todo: Add your website and verify it (your website builder or web designer can help).
Submit your website's sitemap.
Look at it once a month for problems.

bing.title: Bing Places and Bing Webmaster Tools (Bing, Copilot, ChatGPT)
bing.why: Bing powers Copilot's answers, and for local questions ChatGPT searches the web through Bing.
todo: Bing Places: import your Google Business Profile in one step, then check the details.
Bing Webmaster Tools: import your website from Google Search Console.
Webmaster Tools also shows when your pages are cited in Copilot and Bing AI answers.

apple.title: Apple Business Connect (Apple Maps and Siri)
apple.why: iPhone users see your Apple Maps place card when they ask Siri or search Maps.
todo: Claim your place card.
Use exactly the same name, address, phone and hours as above.
Add your booking link and a few photos.

social.title: Instagram and Facebook
social.why: Many clients find businesses here first. A "Book" button takes them straight to your booking page.
todo: Add your profiles in Business details, so they show on your booking page.
Instagram: Edit profile › Action buttons › Book, with your booking link.
Facebook page: add a "Book now" button with your booking link.
Put the booking link in your bio and in WhatsApp Business.

reviews.title: Reviews, a steady routine
reviews.why: Reviews count towards prominence on Maps, and clients read them before booking.
todo: Copy your review link from Google Business Profile ("Ask for reviews").
After a visit, send it to happy clients by WhatsApp. (Hosted Statio asks every client for a review for you.)
Reply to every review, good or bad, within a few days.

help.title: Help
help.intro: How things work, in plain words. The "?" on each screen brings you to its topic.

start.title: Getting started
points: Set up in this order: Business (details and opening hours), Services, Team (their services and shifts), Bookings.
Settings has six parts: Business, Team, Services, Bookings, Website and Get found. Each opens one page with its own cards.
Settings shows a "Getting started" list until the basics are done.
Your booking link and QR code are in Settings › Website: put them on Instagram, Google and WhatsApp.

install.title: Your own installation
points: What you need: a GitHub account (free), Vercel Pro, required ($20 a month: a salon taking real bookings is commercial use, which needs Vercel Pro), a Neon Postgres database (free plan, created inside Vercel), an email sender, and your own domain (about 10–20 € a year).

Email is required (sign-in and online booking use email links): create a free account at resend.com, add your domain there, then put RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM in Vercel (Settings › Environment Variables, where your private keys live) and redeploy. Your own mailbox works too, with SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER and SMTP_PASS. You can also set it here under Settings › Bookings › More options › Client emails, and send yourself a test.

Your domain: in Vercel open Settings › Domains › Add and type your domain. Add the DNS records Vercel shows where you bought the domain (if you bought it in Vercel, it's done). Then set BETTER_AUTH_URL to https://yourdomain.com and redeploy. It can take a few hours to start working.
Updates: open your copy on GitHub and click Sync fork › Update branch. Vercel redeploys by itself and your data stays as it is.
Easiest of all: open your copy in Claude Code and say "Set up my salon". It walks you through every step.

website.title: Your website
points: Services, prices, team, hours and contact come straight from the app: change them once and your website shows it.
Website: tap a section to change its words and photos. Tap Publish changes when you're happy.
Photos: one real photo for the top (wider than tall, at least 1500 × 900) and up to 12 of your work.
Your web address is the one set in Vercel. To use your own domain, add it in Vercel (Settings › Domains). Then follow Get found so Google and AI assistants find you.

booking.title: How clients book online
points: Two ways in: by service, or by professional. Each professional also has their own link (Team › their page).
Times appear only once the services are chosen: their durations add up, plus any clean-up time.
Clients sign in with an email link (no password) and leave a mobile number.
Returning clients see "Book again". If a day is full, the page offers the next free time.
Before confirming, clients see a summary with the price and your cancellation rule.

times.title: Recommended times
points: Some times get a sparkle badge: right before or after a booking and the first time of an empty day. Clients can still pick any time.
Choose how times are offered: recommend times that fill gaps (default), show only those, or show all alike.
Also in Bookings › More options: daily limit, start times every X minutes, minimum notice.

rules.title: Approvals and the safety net
points: Confirm bookings automatically, or approve each new client's first booking yourself.
Safety net: new clients can only hold a few future bookings, and clients with no-shows need your approval.
Clients can cancel for free up to the time you set.
Optional questions for new clients and your welcome message are in Bookings › More options.

hours.title: Opening hours, working hours and holidays
points: Opening hours: when the business is open (Settings › Business). Working hours: when each person works (Team). Clients can book only where both overlap.
Closed days: add a date or a range. Online booking stops and those days disappear from the booking page.
Public holidays: pick your country and region, untick the days you work, add the rest. Local town holidays you add by hand.
How far ahead clients can book is in Bookings › More options, in weeks.

clients.title: Clients
points: Everyone who books becomes a client; walk-in guests don't (see Walk-ins).
Filters: overdue, due soon, new, regulars, birthdays. The summary shows where new clients come from.
A client's page has notes, their usual person and service, preferred day, colour history and messages sent.
Owners and managers can merge duplicates, and erase a client's data on request (their visits stay, without a name).
Clients belong to the salon. Someone with "Owns their clients" keeps those whose first visit was with them.

dueBack.title: When a client is due back
points: Each service has a standard "come back in". At checkout the professional can choose a different one for this client.
After 3 visits the app learns the client's own rhythm. You can also set it by hand on their page.
"Due soon" from 80% of their usual interval, "Overdue" after it. Clients › Overdue lists them, with a WhatsApp message in one tap.

guests.title: Walk-ins and guests
points: New booking › Walk-in books any time, even outside hours or over another visit.
"Guest, no client record" is for one-off visitors: the visit counts, but no client is created.
If a guest wants to come back, open the visit and tap "Save as client".

colour.title: Colour card and patch test
points: Each service can "Keep a colour card" and "Ask for a patch test" (Services › edit).
Online, clients must tick the patch-test confirmation. For visits you book, tap "Client confirmed" on the visit.
Write the formula on the visit; next time, "Use the same formula". The client page shows their colour history.

offers.title: Offers
points: Quiet hours: % off on chosen days and times, shown to everyone on the booking page. Use Share to post it.
Personal offers: pick clients and send by WhatsApp, SMS or email.
Refer a friend: each client gets their own link. The friend gets a discount on their first visit, the client who referred them on their next one.

staff.title: Team and access
points: Team has two tabs: People (each person's details, services, hours and access) and Shifts (who works when).
Add a person with their services (and their own time per service if it differs) and working hours.
Access levels: Owner, Manager, Stylist, Front desk, Chair renter, with exceptions per area if needed.
Invite them with a personal link (valid 7 days, one use); they choose their own password. "Reset sign-in" signs them out everywhere.
Each person has their own booking link to share with their clients.

found.title: Get found
points: Use exactly the same name, address, phone and hours everywhere.
Follow the checklist: website, Google Business Profile, Search Console, Bing, Apple, Instagram and Facebook, reviews.
Your booking page already tells search engines your details. Nobody can promise a top position.

money.title: Finances
points: Profit for a day, a week or a month: income minus expenses, compared with the period before.
Income › Services: what clients paid for finished visits, by staff and by service. Chair renters' clients pay them, so the salon counts their chair rent instead (Income › Chair rent).
Expenses: staff pay (commissions and salaries from each staff page) and your regular costs (rent, electricity…), added under Expenses.
Regular costs and chair rent count on the day they're due, like your bank statement; salaries on the last day of the month.
If past visits aren't finished, their money is missing: Finances tells you and links to them.
"Export" gives you the month's numbers as a spreadsheet.

shop.title: Shop
points: Products: add them with a price, and a photo if you like. Clients reserve them on your website or when they book, then pick them up and pay at the salon.
Featured (★): up to 3 products on your website's home page, with a link to your shop page with all of them. They're also suggested to clients after they pick a time when booking.
Products added to a booking show on the visit and go on the bill when you charge it; untick what they didn't take. Requests from the website wait in Requests.

Stock & reorder: the stock goes down when a product is charged. Set a minimum and the days a delivery takes, and it shows in To reorder in time, with how many to order and the order written for your supplier.
For salon use: colour, wax and other supplies you use but don't sell. They're only for stock and reordering.
Finances counts what was charged under Income › Products, with the margin when cost prices are set.

reviews.title: Reviews
points: A couple of hours after a finished visit, every client with an email gets the same "How was your visit?" email (at most once every 90 days; turn it on or off in Reviews › Settings).
They give 1 to 5 stars and a few words on your website, and say whether you may show it. After sending, everyone is offered to post it on Google too.
New reviews wait in Tools › Reviews: show the ones you like on your website, hide others, and reply in public if you want.
Your website's Reviews section shows the average of the reviews you show, and with "Rating with quotes", the reviews themselves, scrolling sideways when there are more than 3.

print.title: Posters, flyers and cards
points: Settings › Print materials makes counter cards, posters, a window poster, flyers, a square sticker and business cards with your QR code, in A sizes or US sizes.
Pick a design (Photo, Logo or Simple), what the QR is for (save you in their phone, book, or leave a Google review) and what to show (hours, address, phone, WhatsApp, offer…).
They're made from your current logo, cover photo, colours and fonts: change them anytime and download again.
"Download PDF for printing" gives the exact size with 3 mm bleed and crop marks, ready for any print shop. The picture (PNG) is for WhatsApp or Instagram.

todo.title: Tasks
points: Today shows what needs you now: visits to close, requests, reviews, clients due back and your own to-dos.
A card goes away when its work is done. "Later" hides it until tomorrow.
Close visits from the card in one tap: paid, didn't come, or change. Closed visits get the thank-you and the review ask, and count in Finances.
Add your own to-dos, for you only or for the team, from a given day.
Tasks are on Today: "See all" at the bottom of the card opens every task (Now, Coming up, Put off, Done in the last 30 days). The number next to Today is what needs you now.

assistant.title: Your assistant (AI package)
points: It writes for you, with "Write it for me" on each page: personal invites (Invite clients), replies to reviews (Reviews), service descriptions (Services, open a service) and your website's About text (Website, About). You read and change each text before you send or save it.
Ask it about your salon ("How did this month go?", "Who hasn't come since summer?"). It answers from your own data and shows where to act. It never changes anything.
It writes in your communication style (Informal, Professional or Formal) and the way people speak in your country.
It runs in your salon's own private space. No other salon can use it or see what it writes.
Each month has an allowance. You see the % left, and a To do card warns you at 80%. When it's used up, it rests until the 1st and everything else works as usual.
